entries.title: ledger: payees on line items, psbt payment method, payout records and events; inscription: attribution metadata (ADR-0009)
entries.detail:
LineItem.payee {kind, ref, address xor scriptHex}; PsbtProvider derives the
expected outputs per payee script, evaluates an observed funding transaction
by scripts and values (paid/overpaid/underpaid/pending), polls Esplora by
scripthash, and refuses to let one txid settle two intents. Payout records
are created settled per payee output, listed per order and per payee, shown
on receipts and published as ledger.payout.{status}. Refund availability
reserves pending refunds and refund writes are version-checked. Response
enums become extensible so the contract stays additive (oasdiff clean);
API 1.1.0. SQLite migration 0002 rebuilds payments and adds payouts.

entries.title: inscription: SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY (0x81) by default, re-signed rescue with the user's ephemeral key
entries.detail:
Closes the redirect gap of the 0x83 half-signed reveal: the signature now
commits to both outputs (parent return, child) while still letting the
service attach the parent input. Self-rescue is kept by re-signing a fresh
[commit] -> [child] with K_e, which the user retains in their recovery
bundle. 0x83 stays available as an explicit option for one release; the CLI
'rescue' command documents both paths. 104 inscription tests.

entries.title: catalog-tool: read a submodule's pinned commit from the index, not only HEAD
entries.detail:
A product repo regenerates its catalog in the same commit that bumps the
deps/scribbit pin, so `git ls-tree HEAD` still saw the old (or no) gitlink
and `external.commit` came out stale/null, failing `pnpm catalog --check`
right after the commit. `git ls-files -s` reads the index, which equals HEAD
after a commit and already reflects a staged bump; ls-tree HEAD remains the
fallback. Covered by the external-workspace fixture test.

entries.title: catalog-tool: compile each workspace root's manifest schema in its own Ajv instance
entries.detail:
Product repos carry a copy of schemas/component.schema.json next to the
platform's copy under deps/scribbit/schemas. Both share one `$id`, and a
single Ajv instance rejects the second compile ("schema with key or id ...
already exists"), which made `pnpm validate` fatal in DegentClub/degent and
DegentClub/blockspace. Each root now gets its own instance; a fixture test
writes a stricter nested schema copy and asserts only the external package
is judged by it.

entries.title: Split the monorepo: scribbit becomes the platform repo (ADR-0004)
entries.detail:
Blockspace Holdings' monorepo is split into three repositories under the
DegentClub org, all sharing this git history. This repository keeps the
shared platform (platform/*), the tooling (tools/*), the scribb.it product
(products/scribbit/**), the platform- and scribbit-owned contracts
(platform-events.yaml, scribbit-fees.yaml), schemas, templates and all ADRs.

Removed here and moved to their product repos (a contract lives with the
component that provides it):
- products/degent/**, contracts/openapi/degent-mint.yaml,
  contracts/asyncapi/degent-mint.yaml, ADR-0002 -> DegentClub/degent
  (docs/adr/0002-degent-mint-architecture.md stays as a one-line pointer)
- products/blockspace/**, contracts/openapi/blockspace-collections.yaml
  -> DegentClub/blockspace

Product repos vendor this repository as a git submodule at deps/scribbit
pinned to a commit and list deps/scribbit/platform/* and deps/scribbit/tools/*
in their pnpm-workspace.yaml, so @bsh/* platform packages and the catalog
tool resolve from here.

Catalog tool (tools/catalog): packages under a NESTED workspace root (a
directory between the repo root and the package with its own
pnpm-workspace.yaml, e.g. deps/scribbit) are treated as external:
- validate resolves their manifest-relative paths against the nested root
  and tags findings with group "external" (stats.external counts them);
  outer manifests may consume deps/<name>/contracts/... (schema pattern
  extended)
- boundaries checks outer @bsh imports against depends_on with external
  packages as known targets but never scans external sources
- catalog lists them with external: { repo, commit, root } (from .gitmodules
  and `git ls-tree HEAD <root>`) and rewrites their paths relative to the
  outer repo, so a machine can follow the link to the platform catalog
- codeowners skips them and the contracts they provide
Fixture-based tests in tools/catalog/test/external.test.ts (39 tests total).
